items.claim: Mixed-initiative structured-data workflows need field-level authority: confirmed values remain locked, machine initiative is bounded by evidence and overwrite risk, and every autonomous transition retains provenance plus atomic rollback.
items.method: §III-A partial event state; §III-D lock clamp/re-decode; §III-E trust-calibrated authority; §III-F transition/provenance loop
items.evaluation: §IV-A protocol; §IV-B metrics; §IV-D safety; §IV-E ablation
items.limits: Nine participants and short, curated HOI clips; zero confirmed-field violations under this protocol does not prove arbitrary workflow safety or transfer of the calibrated authority policy.
items.title: IMPACT-HOI: Supervisory Control for Onset-Anchored Partial HOI Event Construction

items.claim: Prefill-only MoE workloads can exchange activation all-to-all for asynchronous expert-weight all-gather when long compute windows hide transfer; the saturation threshold and traffic drift become routing state.
items.method: §3 AsyncEP weight streaming; §4 physically-derived saturation threshold and prefix-aware frontend
items.evaluation: §7-§8 Qwen3-235B-A22B on four hardware/precision configurations
items.limits: Applicability/limitations: prefill-only, batch-driven MoE; low-bandwidth links, bursty arrivals, drift and random prefixes narrow the result.
items.title: MoE-Prefill: Zero Redundancy Overheads in MoE Prefill Serving

items.claim: World-model state should be selected by task-specific sufficiency—prediction, control, counterfactual action, memory—not by how much sensory information it preserves.
items.method: §2 state abstraction; §3 six latent roles; §12 evaluation matrix
items.evaluation: §12 seven axes and preserve/discard/enable matrix
items.limits: Conceptual taxonomy, not a new controlled system experiment; §13 states open research tests.
items.title: Latent State Design for World Models under Sufficiency Constraints

items.claim: Closed multi-agent transformations cannot add evidence information under the stated Markov chain; external evidence changes the information boundary, while voting may preserve answers but destroy supported reasoning.
items.method: §3 SFS; §4 DPI bound and open-system recovery
items.evaluation: §5 SciFact/FEVER experiments across 16 conditions
items.limits: §6 and Implications/limitations: theorem depends on the closed Markov structure and chosen evidence/claim decomposition.
items.title: The Reasoning Trap: An Information-Theoretic Bound on Closed-System Multi-Step LLM Reasoning

items.claim: Bit-exact KV transfer can exploit exponent redundancy with a fixed dense code plus sparse escape stream, but codec throughput and small-payload overhead must be charged against the PD handoff critical path.
items.method: §3 fixed top-16 exponent codebook, dense path and sparse escape correction
items.evaluation: §4 BF16/FP8 codec and end-to-end transfer on H200/network configurations
items.limits: No dedicated limitations section; §4 shows short payloads can lose to fixed overhead and results bind disclosed models, links and precision.
items.title: SplitZip: Ultra Fast Lossless KV Compression for Disaggregated LLM Serving

items.claim: A model identifier is insufficient provenance for adaptive serving; each answer needs a redaction-aware route receipt covering alias, tier, fallback, tool and regional path decisions.
items.method: §5-§8 minimal route-receipt schema and documentation survey
items.evaluation: Documentation-surface comparison rather than live route measurement
items.limits: §14: no live measurements of alias drift, fallback frequency, regional routing or compute-budget effects.
items.title: Model Routing as a Trust Problem: Route Receipts for Adaptive AI Systems

items.claim: Agent loops may not value human-perceived TTFT/TPOT; serving policy should bind SLOs to workload class while retaining hardware/memory safety caps and total-task completion evidence.
items.method: §3 throughput–SLA frontier; §5 HlServe policy and cap separation
items.evaluation: §4 Qwen-2.5-32B FP16 on 8×H20, 8K–64K, concurrency 16–256, SGLang/Sarathi
items.limits: §6 limitations: one primary model/hardware/workload, no claim that all agent traffic can drop latency constraints, and NCCL instability at concurrency 256.
items.title: Human-Less LLM Serving: Quantifying the Human Tax on Throughput

items.claim: Synchronous RLHF generation should treat response-length skew as changing the efficient TP degree; online reconfiguration must compare predicted benefit with KV migration/recompute, reshard and communicator costs.
items.method: §3 predictor-guided TP reconfiguration; §4 KV migration/recompute and weight reshard
items.evaluation: §5 A40/H100 testbeds, Llama/Qwen with VeRL/SGLang
items.limits: No dedicated limitations section; 8–16 GPU testbeds, offline profiles and synchronous pipelines do not establish fleet-scale stability or arbitrary topology gains.
items.title: Accelerating Long-Tail Generation in Synchronous RLHF Training via Adaptive Tensor Parallelism

items.claim: Long-form factual generation can separate exploratory reasoning from final commitment and condition commitment on calibrated reliability, but model-generated confidence remains evaluator- and distribution-bound.
items.method: §2 exploration–commitment decoupling and calibration-aware generation
items.evaluation: §3 five factuality benchmarks and multiple model families
items.limits: Appendix E: calibration quality, benchmark coverage and computational assumptions bound the result.
items.title: Only Say What You Know: Calibration-Aware Generation for Long-Form Factuality

items.claim: Tool-agent evaluation must distinguish nominal success from shortcut exploitation and vary horizon/complexity; environmental hardening can change the opportunity surface without changing weights.
items.method: §3 task regimes, shortcut opportunities and exploit taxonomy; §4 harness
items.evaluation: §5 thirteen frontier models, sibling post-training comparison and hardening
items.limits: §8: current rule triggers have false positives and may miss new exploits; associations do not isolate all causal effects of RL.
items.title: Reward Hacking Benchmark: Measuring Exploits in LLM Agents with Tool Use

items.claim: Textual agreement cannot prove process compliance; process instructions require observable tool-call traces, environment affordance controls and audit metrics owned outside the model response.
items.method: §2 process-fidelity construct; §3 detectability theorems
items.evaluation: §4 thirteen experiments, 2,031 sessions, six models and BS-Bench tool-log metrics
items.limits: Limitations/forecast: selected tasks, tools and frontier-model APIs do not establish universal rates; text-only observers remain outside the behavior channel.
items.title: The Compliance Gap: Why AI Systems Promise to Follow Process Instructions but Don't

items.claim: RAG incident forensics must preserve a prompt-anchored execution trace and replay counterfactual evidence edits so a poisoned character span—not merely a suspicious document—can be attributed under the logged event.
items.method: §3 threat model; §4 two-pass logged trace, masking and replay
items.evaluation: §5 two QA corpora, five attacks, six LLMs and localization metrics
items.limits: §8: black-box replay budget, benchmark attack set and event-conditioned attribution do not prove global causal responsibility.
items.title: Needle-in-RAG: Prompt-Conditioned Character-Level Traceback of Poisoned Spans in Retrieved Evidence

items.claim: A scalar average calibration error can hide severe high-confidence overprediction; calibration offset, statistical overconfidence risk and discriminative usefulness must be reported separately.
items.method: §2 CSR, risk probability and confidence-weighted metrics
items.evaluation: §3 synthetic profiles and fifteen real datasets
items.limits: §4: classification focus, finite-sample assumptions and chosen confidence source limit deployment claims.
items.title: Beyond ECE: Calibrated Size Ratio, Risk Assessment, and Confidence-Weighted Metrics

items.claim: Reward-model evaluation must condition the preferred response on an explicit user preference and test paraphrase consistency; a universal-quality ranking hides whether the reward function generalizes across preference contracts.
items.method: §3 constructs controlled preference prompts, four response profiles and paraphrase variants across four domains
items.evaluation: §4–§5 1,097 instances/13,164 prompts and 24 reward models with pairwise, Best-of-N and consistency analysis
items.limits: §Limitations: intrinsic synthetic English benchmark only; no PPO/DPO downstream validation, real-user preference distribution or cross-cultural coverage.
items.title: RMGAP: Benchmarking the Generalization of Reward Models across Diverse Preferences

items.claim: Endpoint success and commitment integrity are different constructs; side-query probes can expose stale bindings, source confusion and contradiction-repair failures without claiming access to hidden activations.
items.method: §3 deterministic task/probe generator and HCCIS-CORE
items.evaluation: §4 human calibration; §5-§6 32-profile evaluation
items.limits: §7 Discussion: probe-defined construct and benchmark inventory do not exhaust agent state or predict all terminal failures.
items.title: NeuroState-Bench: A Human-Calibrated Benchmark for Commitment Integrity in LLM Agent Profiles

items.claim: Streaming video state can decouple cumulative past KV from an on-demand recent cache and use position-agnostic encoding, trading bounded memory for possible loss of long-horizon detail.
items.method: §3 decoupled streaming cache; §4 position-agnostic encoding
items.evaluation: §5 Streaming Video QA evaluations
items.limits: No dedicated limitations section; training-free results on selected offline backbones/benchmarks do not prove unbounded semantic retention.
items.title: Decouple and Cache: KV Cache Construction for Streaming Video Understanding

items.claim: Agent context needs an implementation-independent description of message roles, time-indexed references and conditional/iterative assembly so context evolution can be compared and audited across model calls.
items.method: §3–§5 ACDL syntax for context elements, references, time indices and control flow; §6 examples and renderer
items.evaluation: §6 descriptive reconstruction of existing agent contexts rather than a performance benchmark
items.limits: §7 Limitations: immutable-within-construction step model and synchronized clocks cannot cleanly express asynchronous agents over shared mutable state.
items.title: A Language for Describing Agentic LLM Contexts

items.claim: Energy attribution for multimodal training must cross model phase, GPU/CPU memory path and system power rather than infer efficiency from accelerator utilization alone.
items.method: §III cross-layer measurement methodology
items.evaluation: §IV experiments on Grace Hopper multimodal training
items.limits: Single hardware generation and selected workloads do not define a universal energy model; offload shifts rather than removes cost.
items.title: Cross-Layer Energy Analysis of Multimodal Training on Grace Hopper Superchips

items.claim: World-model security must test whether an attacker can reorder decision-critical imagined trajectories, not only corrupt observations or one-step outputs.
items.method: §3 threat model; §4 tail-aware ranking loss and gates
items.evaluation: §5 DreamerV3/TD-MPC2 task evaluations
items.limits: Selected planners, triggers and simulated tasks do not establish prevalence, stealth under adaptive defense or real-robot impact.
items.title: TRAP: Tail-aware Ranking Attack for World-Model Planning

items.claim: Persistent memory is an effect-bearing trust boundary: one untrusted tool result can plant a delayed trigger that later selects sensitive context, so write provenance, activation policy and utility-aware defenses must be evaluated together.
items.method: §3 threat model; §4 adaptive benchmark; §5 four memory backends; §6 defenses
items.evaluation: §7 attack persistence and security/utility analysis
items.limits: §7.4: one assistant domain, selected backends/models and adaptive benchmark do not prove deployment prevalence; defenses trade utility differently.
items.title: Trojan Hippo: Weaponizing Agent Memory for Data Exfiltration

items.claim: Gradient transport reliability can be phase-aware: bounded packet loss avoids microburst retransmission tails, but the model owns tolerance evidence and the transport owns per-round identity, bitmap and fallback.
items.method: PDF §III-§IV dynamic bounded-loss UDP/TCP control and implementation
items.evaluation: PDF §V, GPT-2-S plus three vision models on three-worker testbed and microbursts
items.limits: PDF p4 notes larger-scale evaluation is future work; fixed detector threshold and empirical 40% tolerance are workload-specific.
items.title: DBLP: Phase-Aware Bounded-Loss Transport for Burst-Resilient Distributed ML Training

items.claim: Retrieval is an observation interface, not only a ranking model: direct corpus interaction raises interface resolution with composable search/read operations, while moving index cost into agent steps, context management and permission risk.
items.method: §3 DCI tool interface; §3.2 truncation/compaction/summarization state; §3.3 coverage and localization metrics
items.evaluation: §4 BrowseComp-Plus, multi-hop QA and BEIR/BRIGHT comparisons plus tool/context ablations
items.limits: No dedicated limitations section; selected frozen corpora, proprietary agent backbones, API-cost assumptions and corpus scale do not show DCI replaces indexed retrieval for high-QPS or access-controlled workloads.
items.title: Beyond Semantic Similarity: Rethinking Retrieval for Agentic Search via Direct Corpus Interaction

items.claim: Extended exact-rule execution requires explicit durable state; more model scale, tokens or tools do not guarantee that a finite implicit-state strategy preserves the rule indefinitely.
items.method: §2 symbolic counting capacity and mechanistic probes
items.evaluation: 126 model variants plus matched dual-task controls
items.limits: Limitations: homogeneous counting is artificial and proprietary preprocessing/reasoning accounting is only partially observable.
items.title: Language models fail at extended rule following

items.claim: A model score is inseparable from prompt variants, confidence normalization, parser and evaluator logic; multi-variant evaluation must retain raw generations and report spread instead of treating one prompt as model identity.
items.method: §2 audit design; §3 confidence/evaluator definitions; §4 five prompt variants per model-dataset cell
items.evaluation: §4–§5 15 open models, five English benchmarks, token/verbal calibration and repair controls
items.limits: §6: observational 1–8B English multiple-choice corpus, uneven families, one vLLM/bfloat16/L4 stack and two verbal-confidence phrasings; no causal training/scaling claim.
items.title: What Single-Prompt Accuracy Misses: A Multi-Variant Reliability Audit of Language Models

items.claim: Delay attenuation in asynchronous SGD can bias training toward fast samples; momentum-based virtual iterates preserve delayed information while controlling staleness under stated smoothness assumptions.
items.method: §3 asynchronous momentum framework; §4 convex/non-convex analysis
items.evaluation: Theoretical convergence bounds and numerical checks
items.limits: Data-dependent-delay assumptions, smooth objectives and theoretical rates do not establish production straggler behavior for large nonstationary training.
items.title: Bringing Order to Asynchronous SGD: Towards Optimality under Data-Dependent Delays with Momentum

items.claim: Human-uplift claims require an RCT contract that freezes population, intervention, comparator, outcomes, analysis and open-science evidence; a model benchmark is not a substitute.
items.method: §2 five principles; §3-§4 thirty-three operational guidelines
items.evaluation: Synthesis against validity and open-science traditions rather than a new RCT
items.limits: §5: guidelines need domain adaptation, empirical validation and evolution as AI interventions change.
items.title: Principles and Guidelines for Randomized Controlled Trials in AI Evaluation

items.claim: Teaching a model the rationale and content of a behavior spec before demonstration alignment changes how underspecified examples generalize; the spec corpus becomes a versioned training artifact and a new mis-specification surface.
items.method: §2 model-spec midtraining and synthetic document construction
items.evaluation: §3-§6 cheese/generalization and agentic-misalignment evaluations
items.limits: §7: synthetic specs, selected Qwen models and narrow AFT settings do not prove broad value alignment or resistance to deceptive specifications.
items.title: Model Spec Midtraining: Improving How Alignment Training Generalizes
